youtube.title: This Bridge Started Moving the Day It Opened. 4 Months Later It Tore Itself Apart
youtube.description:
The Tacoma Narrows Bridge opened on 1 July 1940. To save money, its designer replaced deep 25-foot trusses with 8-foot girders, cutting the cost from $11 million to $8 million. The deck bounced in the wind from the first day; workers called it Galloping Gertie. On 7 November 1940, in a 40 mph wind, it twisted itself apart and fell into Puget Sound. No person died; the only victim was a cocker spaniel named Tubby.

📂 Case File #050: Galloping Gertie

Sources: APS News, "November 7, 1940: Collapse of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge" https://www.aps.org/apsnews/2016/11/collapse-of-tacoma-narrows-bridge ; Live Science, "The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapses" https://www.livescience.com/technology/engineering/science-history-the-tacoma-narrows-bridge-collapses-forcing-a-complete-rethink-in-structural-engineering-nov-7-1940
Images: University of Washington Libraries (public domain); 1940 collapse film stills via Wikimedia Commons.
